rules.name: Dogged
rules.description: All regular and veteran Canadian infantry units may be upgraded to Stubborn for +1pts per man. All inexperienced Canadian infantry units may be Green for +1pts per man.

rules.name: Hate the SS
rules.description: Canadian troops are Fanatics when fighting in Close Quarters against SS units.

rules.name: Canadian Army
rules.description: All HQ and infantry units in the army use the Canadian special rules except for Hate the SS.

rules.name: Limited Battle Experience
rules.description: No units in the list may be selected as Veteran.

rules.name: Been There, Done That
rules.description: All infantry, headquarters, and artillery units in the list must be taken as Veterans. Dogged units must be upgraded to Stubborn.

rules.name: Comrades in Arms
rules.description: The Canadian airborne units worked closely with their British counterparts. You may include one unit of either British Airborne Pathfinders or British Airborne Royal Engineers found on page 136 of the D-Day: Overlord book.

rules.name: Devil's Brigade Veterans
rules.description: Any infantry units may be upgraded to tough fighters for +1pt per model.

rules.name: Artillery Command Vehicle
rules.description: If field artillery and Centaur platoons (i.e. not anti-tank platoons), the command vehicle may be upgraded to a spotter for +40pts. This allows the other vehicles in the platoon to use the command vehicle's line of sight for indirect fire each turn. The command vehicle may not fire any turrent mounted weapons the same turn as being used as a spotter.

rules.name: Troop Integrity
rules.description: Aside from the command vehice, all other vehicles in the platoon (not including transports and tows) must be of the same type.

rules.name: Bombardment
rules.description: Due to British tactical doctrine which relied on extensive Preparatory Bombardment British and Commonwealth roll 2 dice for each target unit, choosing the best die roll as a result.

rules.name: Artillery Support
rules.description: Canadian platoons may include one free Artillery Forward Observer. Platoons may purchase another Artillery Forward Observer if desired.

rules.name: Canadian Infantry Division 1945
rules.description: Ram Cruiser Mk II must take flamethrower option. Ronsons: Canadian platoons may select a Wasp IIC or a Ram Badger as an additional choice that does not count against the number of Tanks, Tank Destroyers, Self-Propelled Artillery, and Anti-Aircraft Vehicles allowed in the selector. May not take a twin Bren AA gun

rules.name: Canadian 1st Division, Italy
rules.description: Canadian HQ and infantry weapons teams use the Tough as Old Boots national characteristic. One other national characteristic may be picked for non-Canadian Infantry sections in the Reeinfroced Platoon. If Canadian infantry units are selected in non-Canadian reinforced platoons they keep the Tough as Old Boots characteristic rather than the national characteristic chosen for that force.

rules.name: Canadian Infantry Division 1943-44
rules.description: M4A4 Sherman V Flail - June 1944 onwards only, Cruiser Tank Mk VIII Centaur CS - June 1944 onwards only, Archer SP 17-Pdr - October 1944 onwards only, Wasp IIC - August 1944 onwards only, May not take a twin Bren AA gun

sharedRules.name: Armoured Recon
sharedRules.description: The squad must have one of the following vehicles purchased as a transport: M5 Half Track, M3 White Scout Car, or C15TA Armoured Truck.

sharedRules.name: LZ Signals
sharedRules.description: If you deploy at least one unit of Pathfinders on the table before the game states (i.e. the Pathfinders are not in the first wave or in reserve), then any friendly paratroopers and glider units in reserve may re-roll failed Order tests to come onto the table.

sharedRules.name: CANLOAN
sharedRules.description: Canadian officers do not use National Characteristics. Instead, they always have the Dogged and Hate the SS rules.

sharedRules.name: Armoured OP
sharedRules.description: An Armoured OP Vehicle is a transport vehicle, but may only transport an Artillery Forward Observer team of up to three models. Provided the Armoured OP vehicle has not yet been given an order, an embarked Artillery Forward Observer team can be given a Fire order to allow them to call in their artillery mission using the line of sight of the vehicle. As soon as an embarked Artillery Forward Observer Team is given the Fire order, pull another order die and give the vehicle a Down order. If the vehicle has already been given an order die this turn, the Artillery Forward Observer Team is assumed to be busy executing that order and may not call in their artillery mission on that turn.

rules.name: CANLOAN
rules.description: Canadian officers do not use National Characteristics. Instead, they always have the Dogged and Hate the SS rules.

rules.name: Intelligence
rules.description: Once per game, at the beginning of any turn before the first die is drawn from the dice bag. Roll a D6 and apply modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the player activating the Intelligence Officer may choose a die from the bag for the first activation. If both players attempt to activate this ability simultaneously, each must roll 1D6. The higher score wins and immediately uses this ability, but the losing player may attempt to use his ability on another turn instead.

rules.name: Medical Vehicle
rules.description: Being in proximity of an ambulance means that any wounded soldiers nearby have a chance of being treated by a medic or stretcher bearer from amongst the crew of the ambulance .All infantry and artillery units within 6" of the vehicle count as within 6" of a medic.

rules.name: Improvised role

rules.name: Little John Adaptor
rules.description:
+ 1 armour penetration. Cannot fire HE while fitted. 
If you roll a 1 (before modification) when you are rolling to hit then it has broken. The crew must spend one turn outside the vehicle removing the broken adapter before they can fire their main weapon again. Remember it is now  a normal light AT-gun.

rules.name: Small vehicle flamethrower
rules.description: The Wasp's flamethrower is somewhat less powerful than those mounted on larger vehicles, so the range of the weapon is limited to 12" and the number of shots is always reduced by one (i.e. it's 2D6-1)

rules.name: Inspiring Presence
rules.description: Upon receiving his order dice (except for Down), a chaplain may select one friendly unit within 6" and roll a D6, applying the following modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the chaplain may remove 1 pin from the selected unit.

rules.name: Non Combatant
rules.description: The chaplain is there to support the soldiers, not win battles. A chaplain unit cannot be used to claim or contest objectives.

rules.name: Self-defence only
rules.description: Clergymen are not soldiers and will not take part in hostile actions - they cannot fire any weapon, nor assault enemy units. If your chaplain is equipped with a pistol, it can only be used in close quarters if the enemy assaults him (including firing it at the assaulting enemies as a reaction, if applicable).

rules.name: Gun assembly
rules.description: To simulate the fact that the gun was actually transported disassembled, when the gun is unlimbered the artillery unit suffers a pin. When the gun is limbered, the mule team (and consequently the transported artillery unit) suffers a pin.

rules.name: Stubborn (Mule)
rules.description: When taking an order test and doubles are rolled, the mules become stubborn and refuse to cooperate even if the order test was passed. Place the order dice to Down and add 1 pin marker to th eteam. This rule does not apply if Fubar is rolled.
